ℙ(v12≥α)≤2e−αd′/2\mathbb{P}(v_{1}^{2}\geq\alpha)\leq 2e^{-\alpha d^{\prime}/2}

gives the first inequality in (138) with α=(16​R2​n)−1\alpha=(16R^{2}n)^{-1}. Averaging over the conditioning, including the r=0r=0 fibers, proves the claim. ∎

Lemma B.13 (Finite-channel random rotation).

Let UU have the uniform invariant Stiefel distribution on Ortho⁡(d,T)\operatorname{Ortho}(d,T), independently of i.i.d. seeds ξ1,ξ2,…\xi_{1},\xi_{2},\ldots and the private randomness of an adaptive randomized algorithm. Suppose the algorithm makes queries (xt,yt)(x_{t},y_{t}) satisfying ‖xt‖≤R\left\lVert x_{t}\right\rVert\leq R almost surely and observes the canonical responses (121). Put

πN:=max1≤t≤N⁡prog1/4⁡(U⊤​xt).\pi_{N}:=\max_{1\leq t\leq N}\operatorname{prog}_{1/4}(U^{\top}x_{t}).

If the latent kernel is a uniform finite-channel probability-ϖ\varpi zero-chain and d>N+Td>N+T, then

ℙ⁡(πN≥T)≤e2​ϖ​N−T+2​N​T​exp⁡(−d−N−T32​R2​N).\mathbb{P}(\pi_{N}\geq T)\leq e^{2\varpi N-T}+2NT\exp\!\left(-\frac{d-N-T}{32R^{2}N}\right). (139)

The bound does not depend on the finite number mm of vector channels.

Proof.

We separate rare progress from geometric guessing.

Rare progress.

For t∈[N]t\in[N], let

𝒱t:={prog1/4(vt)≤γt−1}.\mathcal{V}_{t}:=\{\operatorname{prog}_{1/4}(v_{t})\leq\gamma_{t-1}\}.

Use the filtration

ℋt:=σ⁡(U,ξ0,ξ1,…,ξt),ℋ0:=σ⁡(U,ξ0).\mathcal{H}_{t}:=\sigma(U,\xi_{0},\xi_{1},\ldots,\xi_{t}),\qquad\mathcal{H}_{0}:=\sigma(U,\xi_{0}). (140)

Because the algorithm is deterministic after fixing ξ0\xi_{0}, UU, and the past seeds, (xt,yt)(x_{t},y_{t}), vtv_{t}, γt−1\gamma_{t-1}, and 𝒱t\mathcal{V}_{t} are ℋt−1\mathcal{H}_{t-1}-measurable. On 𝒱t\mathcal{V}_{t}, (119) gives γt−γt−1∈{0,1}\gamma_{t}-\gamma_{t-1}\in\{0,1\}. If additionally ξt∉E\xi_{t}\notin E, then (120) gives γt=γt−1\gamma_{t}=\gamma_{t-1}. Equivalently,

0≤γt−γt−1≤𝟏{ξt∈E}on 𝒱t.0\leq\gamma_{t}-\gamma_{t-1}\leq\mathbf{1}_{\{\xi_{t}\in E\}}\qquad\text{on }\mathcal{V}_{t}. (141)

For the Bernoulli constructions, the right side is ζt\zeta_{t}. Thus an open gate is necessary for progress on 𝒱t\mathcal{V}_{t}, but need not be sufficient. Freshness of ξt\xi_{t} implies

ℙ(γt−γt−1=1,𝒱t∣ℋt−1)≤ϖ.\mathbb{P}\left(\gamma_{t}-\gamma_{t-1}=1,\mathcal{V}_{t}\mid\mathcal{H}_{t-1}\right)\leq\varpi. (142)

Set ιt:=γt−γt−1\iota_{t}:=\gamma_{t}-\gamma_{t-1}. Iterated conditioning gives

𝔼[e∑t=1Nιt𝟏∩t=1N𝒱t]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[e^{\sum_{t=1}^{N}\iota_{t}}\mathbf{1}_{\cap_{t=1}^{N}\mathcal{V}_{t}}\right] ≤(1−ϖ+ϖ​e)N≤e2​ϖ​N.\displaystyle\leq(1-\varpi+\varpi e)^{N}\leq e^{2\varpi N}.

Hence

ℙ⁡(γN≥T,⋂t=1N𝒱t)≤e2​ϖ​N−T.\mathbb{P}\left(\gamma_{N}\geq T,\bigcap_{t=1}^{N}\mathcal{V}_{t}\right)\leq e^{2\varpi N-T}. (143)

On ∩t𝒱t\cap_{t}\mathcal{V}_{t}, the event {πN≥T}\{\pi_{N}\geq T\} implies {γN≥T}\{\gamma_{N}\geq T\}.

Geometric guessing.

Apply Lemmas B.8 and B.12 with horizon n=Nn=N. Since γt\gamma_{t} is nondecreasing,

⋂i=1N⋂j=1T(𝒢j(i)∪(𝒯j(i−1))c)⊆⋂i=1N𝒱i.\bigcap_{i=1}^{N}\bigcap_{j=1}^{T}\left(\mathcal{G}_{j}^{(i)}\cup(\mathcal{T}_{j}^{(i-1)})^{c}\right)\subseteq\bigcap_{i=1}^{N}\mathcal{V}_{i}. (144)

Indeed, fix ii and j>γi−1j>\gamma_{i-1}. Then j>γq−1j>\gamma_{q-1} for every q≤iq\leq i, so the event on the left of (144) supplies ∩q=1i𝒢j(q)\cap_{q=1}^{i}\mathcal{G}_{j}^{(q)}. Lemma B.8 then gives |⟨uj,xi⟩|≤1/4|\left\langle u_{j},x_{i}\right\rangle|\leq 1/4. This holds for every j>γi−1j>\gamma_{i-1}, which is exactly 𝒱i\mathcal{V}_{i}.

A union bound and Lemma B.12 now give

ℙ⁡([⋂i=1N𝒱i]c)≤2​N​T​exp⁡(−d−N−T32​R2​N).\mathbb{P}\left(\left[\bigcap_{i=1}^{N}\mathcal{V}_{i}\right]^{c}\right)\leq 2NT\exp\!\left(-\frac{d-N-T}{32R^{2}N}\right). (145)

Combining (143) and (145) proves (139). The argument never counts the number of vector channels: on 𝒯j(i−1)\mathcal{T}_{j}^{(i-1)}, every one of them lies in span⁡{u1,…,uj−1}\operatorname{span}\{u_{1},\ldots,u_{j-1}\}, and all non-ambient channels are already determined by the conditioned latent queries and seeds. ∎

Corollary B.14 (Terminal output).

Under the assumptions of Lemma B.13, suppose d>N+1+Td>N+1+T and, after NN calls, the algorithm outputs an σ⁡(ξ0,𝒯N)\sigma(\xi_{0},\mathcal{T}_{N})-measurable point xoutx_{\rm out} with ‖xout‖≤R\left\lVert x_{\rm out}\right\rVert\leq R. Then

ℙ⁡(max⁡{maxt≤N⁡prog1/4⁡(U⊤​xt),prog1/4⁡(U⊤​xout)}≥T)\displaystyle\mathbb{P}\left(\max\left\{\max_{t\leq N}\operatorname{prog}_{1/4}(U^{\top}x_{t}),\operatorname{prog}_{1/4}(U^{\top}x_{\rm out})\right\}\geq T\right)
≤e2​ϖ​N−T+2​(N+1)​T​exp⁡(−d−(N+1)−T32​R2​(N+1)).\displaystyle\qquad\leq e^{2\varpi N-T}+2(N+1)T\exp\!\left(-\frac{d-(N+1)-T}{32R^{2}(N+1)}\right). (146)
Proof.

Set xN+1:=xoutx_{N+1}:=x_{\rm out} and regard it only as an additional point in the geometric argument. No oracle call is made at this point: no new seed is drawn, no response is returned, and the revealed progress is fixed at γN+1:=γN\gamma_{N+1}:=\gamma_{N}. Thus the rare-progress estimate remains exactly e2​ϖ​N−Te^{2\varpi N-T}. Repeat the projection-accumulation, conditional-residual-law, and union bound arguments with the N+1N+1 vectors x1,…,xN,xoutx_{1},\ldots,x_{N},x_{\rm out}. For each jj, on 𝒯j(N)\mathcal{T}_{j}^{(N)}, the quiet-simulation argument in Lemma B.11 reconstructs the transcript from 𝒰j−1(N)\mathcal{U}_{j-1}^{(N)}. The output is therefore measurable from this field on that event. The same conditional-law argument applies to the final point without a new seed. Taking n=N+1n=N+1 in the geometric term gives (146). ∎

Corollary B.15 (Soft projection and known postprocessing).

Let ρ:ℝd→ℝd\rho:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{d} be Borel with ‖ρ⁡(x)‖≤R\left\lVert\rho(x)\right\rVert\leq R for all xx. Let (x,y,o)↦𝖯x,y​(o)(x,y,o)\mapsto\mathsf{P}_{x,y}(o) be a jointly Borel map independent of UU, and suppose the actual response is

𝖯x,y​(𝒪~U​(ρ⁡(x),y,ξ)).\mathsf{P}_{x,y}\!\left(\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}_{U}(\rho(x),y;\xi)\right).

Then Lemma B.13 and Corollary B.14 hold with U⊤​xU^{\top}x replaced by U⊤​ρ​(x)U^{\top}\rho(x).

Proof.

An algorithm interacting with the actual oracle can be simulated by an algorithm interacting with the richer canonical oracle: the simulator queries ρ⁡(x)\rho(x), receives the canonical response, applies the known postprocessing, and passes the result to the original algorithm. At termination it returns ρ⁡(xout)\rho(x_{\rm out}), with no additional call. Joint measurability makes this a valid adaptive simulation. ∎

B.4 The comparison oracle and the first-order benchmark

Proof of Proposition 4.1.

Take the scaled pair (AU,uU)(A_{U},u_{U}) from Proposition B.6, with TT as in (110). For 0<ϖ≤1/20<\varpi\leq 1/2, put Ns:=⌊T/(8​ϖ)⌋N_{\mathrm{s}}:=\lfloor T/(8\varpi)\rfloor and choose

d:=⌈Ns+1+T+32​R2​(Ns+1)​log⁡(64​(Ns+1)​T)⌉.d:=\left\lceil N_{\mathrm{s}}+1+T+32R^{2}(N_{\mathrm{s}}+1)\log\bigl(64(N_{\mathrm{s}}+1)T\bigr)\right\rceil. (147)

Draw UU uniformly from Ortho⁡(d,T)\operatorname{Ortho}(d,T), independently of the algorithm seed and oracle draws. The functions are smooth; their Lipschitz, value, and gap bounds follow from (115)–(117).

At a bounded query r¯∈ℝd\bar{r}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}, write v=U⊤​r¯v=U^{\top}\bar{r} and consider

By Corollary B.3, its two vector channels satisfy Definition B.7 with exceptional event {ζ=1}\{\zeta=1\}. The scalar channel is a Borel function of the latent query vv and the seed, as allowed by that definition. Hence the full response, including the scalar value, is covered by Corollary B.14.

One comparison call at an arbitrary xx is obtained by querying (148) at r¯=ρR​(x/λlb)\bar{r}=\rho_{R}(x/\lambda_{\rm lb}) and returning

B.4.1 Variance and the ordinary first-order lower bound

Lemma B.16 (Variance and the ordinary first-order lower bound).

For each pair in Proposition 4.1, (21) is conditionally unbiased and

Fix UU and condition on the history ℋ\mathcal{H}, which fixes the query xx. The fresh Bernoulli seed satisfies 𝔼⁡[ζ/ϖ]=1\mathbb{E}[\zeta/\varpi]=1, so (21) is conditionally unbiased. Moreover,
